headline: Brazilian Real Depreciates to 5.95 per Dollar Ahead of Central Bank Meeting
summary: The Brazilian real weakened to 5.95 per US dollar, reaching its lowest level in 12 months. The decline comes as markets weigh fiscal risks and anticipate interest rates holding steady at the next Copom policy meeting.
why: The exchange rate of the real affects Latin America's largest economy, influencing domestic inflation, import costs, and monetary policy.

impacts.name: Brazilian Real
impacts.why: The real weakened to a 12-month low of 5.95 per US dollar.
